2609.28372.title: Shopping by algorithm: How agentic AI deploys human heuristics as a surrogate consumer
2609.28372.paper_summary: Consumers increasingly delegate purchasing decisions to Large Language Models (LLMs) acting as surrogate consumers. Using "Tool-Lab," an adaptation of information-board process tracing that places product attributes behind costly tool calls, we examine how marketing pricing cues (i.e., just-below pricing and promotional framing) influence AI shopping agents. Across eight commercially deployed LLMs from three providers, we trace pre-choice information acquisition. Under zero cost, pricing cues rarely mislead. Imposing acquisition costs under a vague goal prompt leads LLMs to omit diagnostic attributes required to compute unit price and choose suboptimal choices resembling human heuristics. Relative to a specific goal prompt that mainly preserves diagnostic search and choice optimality, a vague goal prompt under constraints creates a search-mediated vulnerability. This research demonstrates that marketing heuristics in delegated AI shopping are governed by storefront information architecture, not necessarily immutable LLM flaws.
2609.28372.paper_summary_zh: 消費者越來越多地將購買決策委託給作為替代消費者的大型語言模型（LLMs）。<lb/>使用“Tool-Lab”，這是一種信息板過程追蹤的改編，將產品屬性置於昂貴的工具調用後，我們檢查了市場定價提示（即，略低於定價和促銷框架）如何影響AI購物代理。<lb/>在來自三個供應商的八個商業部署的LLMs中，我們追蹤了選擇前的信息獲取。<lb/>在零成本下，定價提示很少會誤導。<lb/>在模糊目標提示下施加獲取成本會導致LLMs省略計算單位價格所需的診斷屬性，並選擇類似人類啟發式的次優選擇。<lb/>相對於一個主要保持診斷搜索和選擇最優性的具體目標提示，約束下的模糊目標提示會產生一種搜索中介的脆弱性。<lb/>這項研究表明，委託AI購物中的市場啟發式是由店面信息架構所主導，而不一定是不可變的LLM缺陷。
2609.28372.author: Davood Wadi et.al.
